mainTopic: Why יעל did not benefit from סיסרא, and which shoes are fit for חליצה: someone else's, a left sandal, a wooden sandal, and a sandal with צרעת or tied to עבודה זרה.
overview: The גמרא finishes the principle that the good done by the wicked is bad for the righteous. It proves this from God's warning to לבן not to speak to יעקב 'either good or bad.' It explains that סיסרא harmed יעל by putting זוהמא into her, backed by רבי יוחנן's teaching about the נחש and חוה. Then it returns to the משנה. A ברייתא shows that anyone's shoe works for חליצה, as long as it fits the יבם. In a story, רב יוסף tells אביי to give his sandal to the יבם as a gift and objects to the left sandal אביי hands over. The גמרא asks whose view allows a wooden sandal: רבי מאיר, or everyone if it is covered in leather. Two students report רבא differently on a sandal with צרעת, and the גמרא tests the idea that something waiting to be burned counts as already crushed. רבא's final ruling is that a מוסגר, מוחלט, or עבודה זרה sandal should not be used, but a חליצה done with one is valid. The amud ends as he begins the separate case of a sandal offered to an idol.

steps.title: A verse about לבן and יעקב as the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the principle that the good of the wicked is bad for the righteous, and brings the פסוק where God warns לבן not to speak to יעקב 'from good to bad.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [The good of the wicked] is bad for the righteous, as it says: 'Guard yourself, lest you speak with יעקב from good to bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes a sentence that started before this section and brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God warns לבן not to say anything bad to יעקב, and also nothing good. The next steps use the word 'good' in this פסוק to prove the principle.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: is a bad thing for the righteous.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence that started just before: 'the good done by the wicked is bad for the righteous.'

phrases.english: As it is said: 'Guard yourself'
lest you speak with Jacob
either good or bad.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 31:24. God is speaking to לבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִשָּׁמֶר לְךָ פֶּן תְּדַבֵּר עִם יַעֲקֹב מִטּוֹב עַד רָע״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the principle about יעל and סיסרא that the גמרא started before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The principle טובתן של רשעים רעה היא אצל צדיקים

steps.title: Why forbid speaking good?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that forbidding bad speech makes sense, but asks why לבן was also told not to speak good.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he may not speak bad. But good, why not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the פסוק to set up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling לבן not to harm יעקב is easy to understand. Forbidding kind words is surprising, so it needs an explanation, and that explanation will be the principle.

phrases.english: It makes sense that he may not speak bad,
but good, why not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַע — לְחַיֵּי, אֶלָּא טוֹב אַמַּאי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the word 'good' in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would the פסוק forbid לבן from saying good things to יעקב?

steps.title: The good of the wicked is bad for the righteous
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'good' in the פסוק, the גמרא concludes that even the kindness of a wicked person is harmful to a righteous person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: the good of the wicked is bad for the righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question and draws the lesson from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'good' from לבן was also forbidden, his good must count as something bad for יעקב. This proves the principle the גמרא is using to explain יעל.

keyTerms.meaning: The good / kindness of the wicked

steps.whatToRemember: טובתן של רשעים רעה היא אצל צדיקים: even what the wicked give as good is bad for the righteous, proven from 'from good to bad' said to לבן.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this:
the good of the wicked
is bad for the righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 and proves the principle.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The kindness of the wicked counts as harm for the righteous.

steps.title: What harm was there for יעל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: with לבן the harm is clear, since he might mention his idol. But with יעל and סיסרא, what harm is in his 'good'?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense there, since perhaps he would mention to him the name of an idol. But here, what bad is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges whether the principle really fits the case of יעל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With לבן, his kind words could include the name of his עבודה זרה, which would truly hurt יעקב. With יעל, the גמרא cannot see what harm she got from סיסרא, so the proof may not fit her case.

phrases.english: It makes sense there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means לבן speaking to יעקב.

phrases.english: since perhaps he would mention to him
the name of an idol.
But here, what bad is there?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means יעל with סיסרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם, דִּלְמָא מַדְכַּר לֵיהּ שְׁמָא דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges applying the principle from step 3 to יעל.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying טובתן של רשעים רעה to יעל and סיסרא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The harm in לבן's case (mentioning an idol) does not exist in יעל's case, so what harm did she get?

steps.title: He put filth into her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that סיסרא put spiritual filth (זוהמא) into יעל, and that is the harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he puts filth into her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by naming the harm יעל received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harm is not in words but in the relationship itself: a wicked non-Jew passes a spiritual filth into her. So she did not get any real benefit from it.

phrases.english: Because he puts filth into her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different kind of harm that applies in יעל's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יעל gained nothing bad from סיסרא, so the principle does not fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: סיסרא put זוהמא into her, which is a real harm, so his 'good' was bad for her.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on the snake's filth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the נחש put filth into חוה. It ended for ישראל at הר סיני, but not for non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said: When the נחש came upon חוה, he put filth into her. ישראל, who stood at הר סיני, their filth stopped. Non-Jews, who did not stand at הר סיני, their filth did not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its answer with a teaching of רבי יוחנן about where this filth comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The filth began with the נחש and חוה. Standing at הר סיני removed it from ישראל, but non-Jews like סיסרא still carry it. This explains why סיסרא could pass it on to יעל.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Sinai, where the תורה was given

steps.whatToRemember: The harm to יעל was זוהמא: it came from the נחש, ended for ישראל at הר סיני, and remains in non-Jews.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
When the snake came upon Eve
he put filth into her.
Israel, who stood at Mount Sinai,
their filth stopped.
Non-Jews, who did not stand at Mount Sinai,
their filth did not stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 5 by explaining where זוהמא comes from.
steps.raayaObject: That סיסרא, a non-Jew, carries זוהמא that he could pass to יעל
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching about the נחש, חוה and הר סיני

steps.title: Back to the משנה: חליצה with someone else's shoe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if she did חליצה with a shoe that is not his, it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she did חליצה with a shoe that is not his, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the יעל discussion and quotes a new line of the משנה to start a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line opens a new section about which shoe may be used for חליצה. The next step will bring a ברייתא as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: She performed חליצה (removed the יבם's shoe)
Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: If she did חליצה with a shoe
that is not his, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה rules that this חליצה is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה done with a shoe that does not belong to the יבם is valid.

steps.title: The verse says 'his shoe': what about anyone's shoe?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא notes that the פסוק says 'his shoe' and asks where we learn that any person's shoe works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: 'His shoe' teaches me only his own shoe. From where do we know a shoe of any person?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sets up a question from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'His shoe' sounds like it must belong to the יבם. The ברייתא asks for a source for the משנה's ruling that someone else's shoe is fine.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: 'His shoe,'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

phrases.english: I only know his own shoe.
A shoe of any person, from where?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״נַעֲלוֹ״, אֵין לִי אֶלָּא נַעֲלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא as the source for the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does the תורה teach that a shoe not owned by the יבם is valid?

steps.title: 'Shoe' means any shoe
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the פסוק also says just 'shoe', which teaches that any shoe works.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'shoe': a shoe in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question from another word in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides 'his shoe', the תורה also says 'the shoe' without 'his'. This wider wording includes anyone's shoe, which supports the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: A חליצה with anyone's shoe is valid, learned from the plain word 'shoe' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'shoe,'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:10: 'the house of the one whose shoe was removed', with no 'his'.

phrases.english: a shoe in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'shoe' (without 'his') includes any person's shoe.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say 'his shoe'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if any shoe works, what does the word 'his shoe' come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say 'his shoe'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא just said that any shoe works. Now it asks what the word 'his' is for, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 showed that the plain word 'shoe' includes any shoe, even one that is not his. That leaves the word 'his' with nothing to teach. The ברייתא looks for a new job for that word.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your answer is true)
Why does the פסוק say this? (What does this word teach?)

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say 'his shoe'?
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer in step 9, which made the word 'his' seem unneeded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'his' in 'his shoe' teaches, now that it does not teach ownership.

steps.title: 'His shoe' means a shoe that fits him
steps.stepSummary: 'His shoe' means a shoe that fits him. This rules out a shoe that is too big, one that is too small, and a sandal with no heel.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His shoe' means a shoe fitting for him. This excludes a shoe so big he cannot walk in it, a shoe so small it does not cover most of his foot, and a sandal without a heel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that 'his' means 'suited to him'. It then lists three kinds of shoes that do not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'his' does not mean ownership. It means fit. A shoe he cannot walk in, a shoe that covers less than most of his foot, and a sandal with only a sole and no heel are not a proper shoe for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal with only a sole and no heel
Heel (the back part of the shoe)

steps.whatToRemember: Any person's shoe works for חליצה, but it must fit the יבם properly.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'his shoe' as 'a shoe he owns.' Here it means 'a shoe that fits him.'

phrases.english: 'His shoe' means one that is fitting for him.

phrases.aramaic: פְּרָט לְגָדוֹל שֶׁאֵין יָכוֹל לַהֲלוֹךְ בּוֹ,
phrases.english: This excludes a large one that he cannot walk in,

phrases.aramaic: וּפְרָט לְקָטָן שֶׁאֵינוֹ חוֹפֶה רוֹב רַגְלוֹ,
phrases.english: and excludes a small one that does not cover most of his foot,

phrases.aramaic: וּפְרָט לְסַנְדָּל הַמְסוּלְיָים שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עָקֵב.
phrases.english: and excludes a heelless sandal, which has no heel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'His' means a shoe that fits him. It excludes one too big, one too small, and a heelless sandal.

steps.title: Story: אביי gives his left sandal for a חליצה
steps.stepSummary: A יבמה came before רב יוסף. He told אביי to give his sandal, and אביי gave his left one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was standing before רב יוסף, and a יבמה came to do חליצה. רב יוסף said to him: Give him your sandal. He gave him his left sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about a real חליצה. This step sets up the scene for רב יוסף's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story puts the earlier rules into practice. The יבם will use a shoe that is not his own, and in this case a left sandal. Both details will matter in the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Was standing before him (learning from his teacher)
The widow who needs יבום or חליצה

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף,
phrases.english: Abaye was standing before Rav Yosef,
a yevama came to perform ḥalitza.
He said to him: Give him your sandal,
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is telling אביי to give his sandal to the יבם.

phrases.english: he gave him his left sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא to a practical story about using another person's shoe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף told אביי to give his sandal to the יבם for the חליצה, and אביי handed over his left sandal.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a left sandal is only good after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that the חכמים allowed a left sandal only after the fact, not from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Say the חכמים said this after the fact. Did they say it from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges אביי for handing over a left sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said a חליצה done this way still counts once it has happened (דיעבד). That does not mean we may plan to do it this way from the start (לכתחילה). רב יוסף wants the חליצה done the best way.

keyTerms.meaning: After the fact (it counts once done)
From the start (the proper way to plan it)

steps.confusionAlert: דיעבד does not mean 'forbidden.' It means it works if already done, but we should not plan it that way.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵימַר דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן, דִּיעֲבַד,
phrases.english: He said to him: Say that the Sages said it after the fact;
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is speaking to אביי.

phrases.english: did they say it from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַר דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן, דִּיעֲבַד, לְכַתְּחִלָּה מִי אֲמוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to what אביי did in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי giving a left sandal for the חליצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A left sandal is allowed only דיעבד, so it should not be used לכתחילה.

steps.title: אביי: a borrowed sandal is also only after the fact
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a sandal that is not the יבם's own is also only good after the fact. So the whole plan was already דיעבד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, a sandal that is not his is also only allowed after the fact. Did they say it from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי turns רב יוסף's argument back on him. A sandal that is not his own is also only good after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 7 allowed a shoe that is not his in the same 'after the fact' way. Since רב יוסף already chose a sandal that was not the יבם's, the חליצה was already a דיעבד case. Using a left sandal changes nothing.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: Now אביי is answering רב יוסף.

phrases.english: a sandal that is not his, too:
phrases.notes: This is the case from the משנה in step 7.

phrases.english: say that the Sages said it after the fact;
did they say it from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, סַנְדָּל שֶׁאֵין שֶׁלּוֹ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection with a counter-challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's demand that the חליצה be done לכתחילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sandal that is not his is also only דיעבד, so רב יוסף's own instruction was already not לכתחילה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: I meant give it as a gift so it becomes his
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that he meant: give the sandal and transfer ownership to the יבם, so it truly is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I was saying to you: Give it to him and transfer ownership to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains what he really meant by 'give him your sandal.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אביי gives the sandal to the יבם as a gift, it becomes the יבם's own shoe. Then it is no longer a 'shoe that is not his,' and the חליצה is לכתחילה. Only the left sandal problem was left, and that is why רב יוסף objected.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I was telling you

steps.whatToRemember: The best way to do חליצה is with a proper right shoe that belongs to the יבם. If you borrow one, give it to him as a gift first.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I was saying to you:
Give it to him and transfer ownership to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's counter-challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought 'give him your sandal' meant only lending it, which would leave it 'not his.'
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף meant giving it as a gift, so it becomes the יבם's. Only the left sandal was a problem.

steps.title: Which תנא holds a wooden sandal works?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's wooden sandal case and asks whose opinion it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: A wooden sandal: who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which said a wooden sandal is valid. It asks whose view that is, setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that wood counts as a shoe. So the גמרא wants to know which תנא the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose opinion is this)?

phrases.english: A wooden sandal.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה, which says חליצה with a wooden sandal is valid.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a wooden sandal counts as a shoe for חליצה.

steps.title: שמואל: it is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it follows רבי מאיר, who allows an amputee to go out on שבת with his wooden leg. רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is רבי מאיר. As we learned: An amputee may go out with his wooden leg, says רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. He proves it from a משנה about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets an amputee go out with his wooden leg on שבת, because he treats wood as a kind of shoe. רבי יוסי forbids it, so to him wood is not a shoe. Since our משנה counts a wooden sandal as a shoe, it must follow רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: It is Rabbi Meir,
as we learned: An amputee may go out with his wooden leg,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת שבת about going out on שבת.

phrases.english: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei prohibits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who treats a wooden leg as a shoe. It does not follow רבי יוסי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת about an amputee's wooden leg.

steps.title: שמואל's father: a leather-covered wooden sandal, so all agree
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's father says the משנה means a wooden sandal covered in leather. Then everyone agrees it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father says: It means one covered in leather, and everyone agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל's father gives a different answer. He explains the משנה so that it fits every opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wooden sandal is covered in leather, even רבי יוסי would count it as a shoe. So the משנה does not have to follow only רבי מאיר.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to explain the wooden sandal. שמואל says it follows רבי מאיר alone. His father says it is covered in leather, so everyone agrees.

phrases.english: The father of Shmuel says:
It is one covered in leather, and it is the statement of all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer than שמואל to the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה speaks of a leather-covered wooden sandal, which all opinions accept.

steps.title: רב פפי's version: a quarantined sandal works after the fact, a confirmed one does not
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, quoting רבא, says she should not do חליצה with a מוסגר or a מוחלט sandal. After the fact, a מוסגר sandal is valid, but a מוחלט sandal is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: with a sandal that is in quarantine for צרעת, she should not do חליצה. But if she did, her חליצה is valid. With a sandal that was confirmed to have צרעת, she should not do חליצה. And if she did, her חליצה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a sandal that has a sign of צרעת. It splits the case into two stages: מוסגר (still being checked) and מוחלט (confirmed).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both kinds of sandal should not be used in the first place. The difference is after the fact. A מוסגר sandal is still a real sandal, so the חליצה counts. A מוחלט sandal must be burned, so רב פפי treats it as if it were already gone, and the חליצה does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: A sandal with a doubtful sign of צרעת that the כהן puts in quarantine to see what develops
A sandal the כהן has confirmed has צרעת; it must be burned
She should not do חליצה with it (in the first place)
Her חליצה is valid / invalid (after the fact)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sandals start with the same 'don't use it' rule. The only argument is about what happens if she already used it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said in the name of Rava:
A quarantined sandal — she should not do chalitza with it,
phrases.notes: 'Quarantined' means the כהן saw a doubtful mark of צרעת on it and set it aside to wait and see.

phrases.english: but if she did chalitza, her chalitza is valid.
A confirmed sandal — she should not do chalitza with it,
and if she did chalitza, her chalitza is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of which sandals are fit for חליצה, now looking at a sandal with צרעת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מוסגר sandal works for חליצה after the fact. A מוחלט sandal does not, even after the fact.

steps.title: רב פפא's version: both kinds of sandal work after the fact
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports רבא differently: both a מוסגר and a מוחלט sandal should not be used, but after the fact the חליצה is valid with either one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said in the name of רבא: whether the sandal is in quarantine or confirmed, she should not do חליצה with it. But if she did, her חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A second student gives a different report of what רבא said. In his version there is no difference between מוסגר and מוחלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא does not treat a מוחלט sandal as already destroyed. It is still a real sandal until it is actually burned, so the חליצה counts after the fact. The only disagreement with רב פפי is about the מוחלט sandal after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that, the same rule for both

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב פפי (step 19) and רב פפא (this step). The names look almost the same, but their versions of רבא's ruling are different.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said in the name of Rava:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד סַנְדָּל הַמּוּסְגָּר וְאֶחָד סַנְדָּל הַמּוּחְלָט —
phrases.english: Both a quarantined sandal and a confirmed sandal —
she should not do chalitza with it,
but if she did chalitza, her chalitza is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same statement by רבא, disagreeing about the מוחלט sandal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both a מוסגר and a מוחלט sandal work for חליצה after the fact.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about a house with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a מוסגר house makes a person טמא when he touches it from inside. A מוחלט house makes him טמא from inside and from outside. Both make a person טמא if he enters them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: a house in quarantine makes things טמא from the inside. A confirmed house makes things טמא from the inside and from the outside. Both of them make a person טמא when he comes into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה about houses with צרעת as a source to challenge רב פפי. This step only quotes the source; the next step shows how it attacks him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key line is the last one: both kinds of house make a person טמא when he enters. That includes a מוחלט house, which must be torn down. So a מוחלט house still counts as a real 'house'.

keyTerms.meaning: A house with a doubtful sign of צרעת, put in quarantine
From its inside and from its outside (touching the outer walls)
They make a person טמא just by his entering

phrases.english: They challenged: A quarantined house makes one impure from within.
phrases.notes: Touching the house from the inside makes a person טמא.

phrases.english: A confirmed house — from within and from behind.
And both this and that make one impure through entering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source against רב פפי's version from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's ruling that a מוחלט sandal is invalid even after the fact.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats a מוחלט house as a real house for the טומאה of entering. This suggests that something waiting to be destroyed is not treated as already destroyed.

steps.title: If a confirmed item counts as crushed, there would be no house to enter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge. If a מוחלט item is treated as already crushed, then a מוחלט house is not a 'house'. But the פסוק requires entering a house, and the משנה says it still makes a person טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that a confirmed item is treated as if it were crushed, we need 'and one who comes into the house', and there is no house here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the משנה is a problem for רב פפי. If a מוחלט house counted as crushed, entering it could not make a person טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפי's version only makes sense if something that must be burned is treated as already destroyed (כמכתת דמי). The פסוק only makes a person טמא when he enters a 'house'. Since the משנה says a מוחלט house still makes a person טמא this way, it must still count as a house, and that goes against רב פפי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (to say)
It is treated as if it were already crushed or destroyed
'And one who comes into the house', the פסוק about the טומאה of entering a house with צרעת
And it is not there, so the requirement is missing

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument between רב פפי and רב פפא depends on one idea: is something that must be destroyed already treated as destroyed? This challenge tests that idea using the laws of a house with צרעת.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it is considered as if crushed —
phrases.notes: This is the idea behind רב פפי: a confirmed item must be destroyed, so it counts as if it were already crushed.

phrases.english: but we require: "And one who comes into the house,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:46

phrases.english: and there is none!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 21 contradicts רב פפי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea behind רב פפי's version, that a מוחלט item is treated as already crushed (כמכתת דמי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a מוחלט house counted as crushed, there would be no 'house' to enter, and the פסוק's requirement would be missing. Yet the משנה says entering a מוחלט house does make a person טמא.

steps.title: A house is different: the פסוק still calls it a house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a house is a special case. The פסוק says 'and he shall break down the house', so even while it is being torn down it is still called a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is different, because the פסוק says: 'And he shall break down the house.' Even while it is being broken down, it is still called a house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the מוחלט house in step 22. A house is a special case because the פסוק still calls it a 'house'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general, a מוחלט item may be treated as already crushed. A house is different: the פסוק uses the word 'house' at the very moment it is being torn down. So the תורה itself keeps it a 'house' for making people טמא who enter it.

keyTerms.meaning: There it is different: the case you brought is a special case.
'And he shall break down the house'. The פסוק about tearing down a house with צרעת.

steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the idea that a מוחלט item counts as crushed. The house is only an exception because a פסוק says so.

phrases.english: There it is different,
as the verse says: 'And he shall break down the house,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:45

phrases.english: even while it is being broken down, it is called a house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22 by making the house a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case exception based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a מוחלט house still makes people טמא, maybe מוחלט items are not treated as crushed at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The house is an exception. The פסוק calls it a house even while it is being torn down, so the general rule can still stand.

steps.title: A rag with צרעת is measured by its size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a rag of three by three with צרעת makes a pure house טמא once most of it enters. The גמרא suggests this is a מוחלט rag, which would show that a מוחלט item still has a size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a rag that is three by three, even though it is not the size of a כזית, makes a pure house טמא once most of it enters. Isn't this talking about a מוחלט rag?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge the idea that a מוחלט item counts as already crushed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא measures the rag: it must be three by three, and most of it must enter the house. If the rag is מוחלט and we still measure it, then a מוחלט item is not treated as crushed. That goes against רב פפי's version of רבא from step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: A rag or small piece of cloth.
Three by three fingerbreadths: the smallest size of cloth that counts.
An olive-bulk, a common minimum amount in הלכה.
What, is it not...? The גמרא suggests how to read the source.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: מַטְלֵית שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: a rag that is three by three,
phrases.notes: Three fingerbreadths by three, and the rag has a spot of צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: even though it does not have an olive-bulk,
once most of it enters a pure house,
it makes it impure.
What, is it not a confirmed one?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַטְלֵית שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the house was set aside as a special case, the גמרא tries a different source: a rag.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a מוחלט item is treated as already crushed (רב פפי's version of רבא).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא measures a rag that seems to be מוחלט. If it can be measured, it is not treated as crushed.

steps.title: No, the rag is only מוסגר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the ברייתא is talking about a מוסגר rag, not a מוחלט one.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about a quarantined (מוסגר) rag.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by reading the ברייתא as talking about a מוסגר rag.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מוסגר rag is not going to be burned, so nobody says it counts as crushed. Measuring it proves nothing about a מוחלט item.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the suggested reading is rejected.
Quarantined: put aside to wait and see whether the צרעת is real. It is not yet confirmed.

phrases.english: No, a quarantined one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 24's reading that the rag is מוחלט.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the assumption that the ברייתא is about a מוחלט rag.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be about a מוסגר rag, which nobody says is crushed.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: one כזית of the rag is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer by quoting the end of the ברייתא. If the rag is thick, then once a כזית of it enters a pure house, the house becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the last part: if the rag had several olive-bulks, then once a כזית of it entered a pure house, it made it טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a challenge to the 'מוסגר' answer by quoting the end (סיפא) of the same ברייתא. The next step explains why this is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a single כזית of the rag is enough to make the house טמא, even if most of the rag stays outside. This is a different kind of rule from the first part, which needed most of the rag to enter.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your answer is right, then there is a problem.
Say the last part: look at the end of the same source.
Several olive-bulks. The rag is thick, so a small piece of it is already a כזית.

phrases.english: If so,
say the last part:
if it had several olive-bulks,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּכְנַס מִמֶּנָּה כְּזַיִת לְבַיִת טָהוֹר —
phrases.english: once an olive-bulk of it entered a pure house,
it made it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 25's answer using the end of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about a מוסגר rag.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the ברייתא gives a כזית rule that does not seem to fit a מוסגר rag. The next step spells this out.

steps.title: Only a מוחלט rag is compared to a dead person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the challenge. The כזית rule makes sense for a מוחלט rag, because a confirmed מצורע is compared to a dead person. But why would a מוסגר rag be compared to a dead person?
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say the rag is מוחלט: that is because it is compared to a dead person. But if you say it is מוסגר, why should it be compared to a dead person?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge: the כזית rule only fits a מוחלט rag, so the ברייתא must be about a מוחלט rag after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead body makes things טמא with just a כזית. A confirmed מצורע is compared to a dead person (היקש), so a כזית of a מוחלט rag can do the same. There is no such comparison for a מוסגר, so the סיפא must be about a מוחלט rag, and then the רישא probably is too.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say... The first half of a 'this fits, but that does not' argument.
It is compared to a dead person, through a היקש (a comparison the פסוק makes).

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison to a dead person only applies to a confirmed (מוחלט) case, not to a quarantined (מוסגר) one. That difference is the whole point of the challenge.

phrases.english: It works well if you say it is a confirmed one:
that is because it is compared to a dead person.
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:12

phrases.english: But if you say it is a quarantined one,
why should it be compared to a dead person?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the סיפא quoted in step 26 is a problem for the 'מוסגר' answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is about a מוסגר rag (step 25).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כזית rule comes from comparing a confirmed מצורע to a dead person. That comparison only covers a מוחלט case, so the ברייתא must be about a מוחלט rag. Then a מוחלט item is still measured, and is not treated as crushed.

steps.title: A garment with צרעת is a special case because of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the ברייתא is talking about a מוחלט rag. It explains that a garment with צרעת is different, because the פסוק calls it a 'garment' even while it burns.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says: 'And he shall burn the garment.' Even while it is being burned, it is still called a garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 27. It admits that the rag really is מוחלט, and then explains why that does not prove anything about other items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an item that must be burned is treated as if it were already crushed, so it has no real size. But the פסוק 'וְשָׂרַף אֶת הַבֶּגֶד' still calls it a בגד even at the time of burning. So a garment with צרעת keeps its size by a special rule of the פסוק. That special rule does not change the general principle.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: this case is special

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not deny that the rag is מוחלט. It agrees that it is, and says the garment case is an exception because of the פסוק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer protects the general idea that an item that must be destroyed counts as already crushed. It does so by making garments with צרעת a special exception.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quietly agreeing that the rag really is מוחלט. It just says the garment case is special.

phrases.english: for the verse says: 'And he shall burn the garment',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:52

phrases.english: even at the time of burning, it is called a garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27 by admitting the rag is מוחלט and treating the garment as a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case exception based on a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the rag is מוחלט and still makes a house טמא, a מוחלט item must keep its size in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a garment with צרעת keeps its size, because the פסוק still calls it a garment while it burns. The general rule stays in place.

steps.title: Why not learn the sandal law from the garment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a מוחלט garment is still a garment, why not learn from it that a מוחלט sandal is still a shoe for חליצה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: if a מוחלט garment still counts as a garment, let us apply the same idea to a מוחלט sandal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 showed that the תורה treats a מוחלט garment as whole even though it must be burned. If so, a מוחלט sandal should also count as a real shoe, and the חליצה should work.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony of removing the brother-in-law's shoe

phrases.english: So let us learn from it!
phrases.notes: He means: learn from the garment that a מוחלט sandal also still counts as a shoe for חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the special rule of step 28 and tries to apply it to the sandal used for חליצה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפי's version of רבא (step 19), that a חליצה with a מוחלט sandal is invalid even after the fact
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the פסוק shows a מוחלט item still keeps its identity, the same should be true of a מוחלט sandal.

steps.title: We do not learn prohibition laws from impurity laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a rule about טומאה cannot teach a rule in the area of איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not learn a prohibition from impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the garment rule cannot be carried over to the sandal, because the two belong to different areas of הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The garment rule comes from the laws of טומאה. The question about using a מוחלט sandal is a question of איסור. The גמרא says these areas cannot be compared, so the special garment rule stays only in טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Prohibition: what is forbidden or allowed
We do not learn (one from the other)

phrases.english: A prohibition from impurity
we do not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks the comparison suggested in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different areas of הלכה cannot be compared
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The garment rule from טומאה should apply to the sandal too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The garment rule stays inside טומאה. It cannot teach anything about a מוחלט sandal.

steps.title: רבא's final ruling on problem sandals
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one should not do חליצה with a מוסגר, מוחלט, or עבודה זרה sandal, but if she did, the חליצה is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that for a מוסגר sandal, a מוחלט sandal, and a sandal of עבודה זרה, she should not do חליצה with them. But if she did, her חליצה is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final practical הלכה for sandals with a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ahead of time, she should not use any of these three sandals. After the fact, though, the חליצה still works with all of them, even the מוחלט one. So the ruling separates what we do from the start from what counts once it is done.

keyTerms.meaning: Quarantined: placed under watch for צרעת
She should not do חליצה (from the start)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: with a מוסגר, מוחלט, or עבודה זרה sandal, don't do חליצה from the start. But if it was done, it is valid.

phrases.english: רבא said: The הלכה is:
whether a quarantined sandal,
or a confirmed sandal,
or a sandal of idol worship —
phrases.notes: A sandal that was put on an idol.

phrases.english: she should not do חליצה with it,
but if she did חליצה, her חליצה is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth, רבא gives the final practical ruling. It matches רב פפא's version (step 20), since even a מוחלט sandal is valid after the fact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the start, do not do חליצה with a מוסגר, מוחלט, or עבודה זרה sandal. After the fact, it is valid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three problem sandals are not to be used from the start, but they work after the fact.

steps.title: Opening the case of a sandal offered to an idol
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a new, different case: a sandal that was brought as an offering to an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sandal of an offering to idol worship...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא starts a new case, and its ruling comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sandal is different from the one in step 31. It was not just placed on an idol. It was brought to the idol as a gift. רבא is separating it out, which hints that its ruling will be different.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to an idol

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the 'sandal of עבודה זרה' in step 31. This one is an offering given to the idol, which is a separate category.

phrases.english: But one of an offering of idol worship,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's ruling by introducing a different case to be set apart from the three sandals of step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a separate ruling for a sandal used as an offering to an idol. The ruling itself comes on the next amud.
